result.topic_en: Euler argues that the equation for a column buckling under its own weight is correct, but its absurd consequence comes from assuming the top end A is free, whereas the real problem requires both ends A and B to be held on the vertical line AB.

items.quote: pro quovis columnarum robore certam altitudinem aſſignari poſſe, quam ſi ſuperent, certe proprio ponderi ſuccumberent
items.english: For any strength of columns a definite height can be assigned which, if they exceed it, they will certainly collapse under their own weight.

items.quote: Sin autem iſta circumſtantia praetermitteretur et ſupremo termino A plena libertas relinqueretur, nihil prorſus abſurdi in illa curua mirabili deprehendetur, ſed potius ſemper eiusmodi caſus aſſignari poterunt, quae cum iſta curua pulcherrime conueniant
items.english: But if this circumstance were disregarded and the top end A were left completely free, nothing absurd at all would be found in that remarkable curve; rather, cases can always be assigned that agree very well with that curve.
